title: The Ring That Rolled Away
story:
The ground past the outer fence was not like the dirt of the Great Canopy, nor like the fine dust of the Whispering Flats. He had never walked on stone that felt so deliberate. He had never smelled air that tasted of toasted flour and dry iron. He had never heard silence broken by so many small, steady clicks. Between his fingers, the heavy metal ring felt cold, a smooth comfort as he crept closer to the nearest wooden structure.

A sharp clatter from around the corner startled him—a sudden, bright clang of metal on metal. James flinched, his fingers loosening. The ring slipped from his grasp, striking the gravel with a hollow chime before bounding down a smooth concrete slope. James lunged forward, reaching out a paw, but the ring spun furiously on its edge, teetering across the rim of an iron storm grate before dropping through the bars with a faint, final splash in the deep dark below. It was gone.

Before James could even look into the shadows beneath the grate, a heavy wooden door groaned on its hinges. Two long shadows stretched across the sunlit yard. From around the corner stepped a figure taller than any creature James had ever seen standing upright. It wore faded blue cloth draped over its limbs and moved with slow, heavy steps, carrying a woven basket of green leaves.

James shrank back behind a stack of weathered wooden crates, holding his breath. He watched the human pause, wipe a brow with the back of a bare hand, and exhale a long, quiet sigh into the afternoon warmth. The ring was lost, swallowed by the subterranean dark, but right in front of him stood the great mystery he had journeyed across the flats to find.
location: Behind a stack of wooden crates at the edge of a human yard
